UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
PLAINTIFF'S OFFER OF RESOLUTION
Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine offers to dismiss with prejudice his claims in this action
against the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children ("NCME") and Katie Hall, and to
release NCMEC's personnel, on the following terms. This Offer does not extend to Meta
Platforms, Inc.
1.
The deposition. NCMEC will produce one witness under Federal Rule of Civil
Procedure 30(b)(6) for an examination not to exceed sixty minutes on the record. The examination
is conducted by remote means and recorded stenographically and by video. Plaintiff pays the
reporter and the videographer.
2.
The questions. The witness will answer each of the following, and reasonable
follow-up to each:
1

(a)
Does NCMEC hold the two CyberTipline reports its April 22, 2026 letters
identify?
(b)
On what date did NCMEC receive each report, and who submitted it?
(c)
Did Meta Platforms, Inc. submit either report?
(d)
Does either report, as NCMEC originally received it, contain the name "Marvelle
J. Ballentine"?
(e)
If that name appears in any NCMEC record associated with either report, when
and how did it get there?
(1)
What did NCMEC review before it sent the letters?
No question will seek the content of any reported image or file or the identity of any person
other than Plaintiff and the submitter.
What is not required. No payment. No admission of liability. No settlement
conference. No particular answer. NCMEC may maintain every position it has taken in this action.
Nothing is required of Hall.
Performance. NCMEC performs when its witness gives a direct answer, on the
record and under oath, to each question in Paragraph 2. None of the following is performance: an
appearance without answers; an invocation of any privilege against self-incrimination; a statement
that the witness does not know or was not prepared; a refusal or an instruction not to answer on
any ground, including privilege, confidentiality, or statute. A refusal is not a breach. It earns no
dismissal. Time spent on objections, colloquy, and non-responsive answers does not count against
the sixty minutes. If the witness answers that either report contains the name, NCMEC will show
Plaintiff that portion of the report at the examination, with any image and any other person's
information removed
2

Dismissal and release. Within seven days after Plaintiff receives the certified
transcript of a performed examination, Plaintiff will file a notice dismissing with prejudice all of
his claims in this action against NCMEC and Hall under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i), each party to bear its
own costs and fees. If the Court requires a motion, Plaintiff will move under Rule 21 within the
same period. On that dismissal, Plaintiff releases NCMEC, Hall, and every current and former
officer, director, employee, and agent of NCMEC from any and all claims arising from or relating
to the April 22, 2026 letters, the CyberTipline reports the letters identify, and the matters alleged
in this action. The obligation arises on performance. It does not arise on acceptance.
Acceptance. NCMEC accepts by filing a notice of acceptance, signed by counsel
of record, on the public docket of this action before expiration. That filing is NCMEC's stipulation
to the examination under Rules 26(d)(1), 29(a), and 30(a)(2)(A)(iii). The examination will be held
within thirty days after acceptance. Plaintiff will give every party fourteen days' notice of it.
Silence is not acceptance. A counterproposal is not acceptance.
Effective date and expiration. This Offer takes effect on service. It does not
depend on any ruling on the Motion to which it is attached. It expires at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
on December 9, 2026.
8.
Use. Plaintiff agrees to no restriction on the use of the transcript or the video record,
subject to any court order or statute.

9.
Meta is not released. This Offer does not dismiss or release any claim against Meta
Platforms, Inc., in this action or in any other. No person is released for conduct undertaken for or
on behalf of Meta Platforms, Inc. Plaintiff's claims against Meta continue.
Date: November 16, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
1520 Belle View Blvd, Ste. #5847
Alexandria, Virginia 22307
(407) 794-6503
jayballentine@protonmail.com
4

CERTIPICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that on November 16, 2026, I submitted the following documents to the Clerk of
Court for filing through the Court's Electronic Document Submission System (EDSS):
Exhibit A, Plaintiff's Offer of Resolution, with its Certificate of Service, Local
Civil Rule 83.1(N) Certification, and Generative Artificial Intelligence Disclosure and Citation
Certification.
Counsel of record for Defendants National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, Katie
Hall, and Meta Platforms, Inc. are registered users of the Court's Case Management/Electronic
Case Filing (CM/ECF) system. Upon the Clerk's docketing of the submission, the CM/ECF system
will transmit a Notice of Electronic Filing to each of them, and service will be made through that
means under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 5(b)(2)(E). EDSS submission is not itself service.
Date: November 16, 2026
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
